structure.note: One class of ordinary shares with one vote each. The 20-F's beneficial ownership table lists no holder of 5% or more as of May 18, 2026; Joseph C. Tsai (1.5%) is the largest listed. The company states it is not aware of any arrangement that may later result in a change of control. Control rests partly outside share ownership: under the Articles, 'the Alibaba Partnership has the exclusive right to nominate or, in limited situations, appoint, up to a simple majority of the members of our board of directors', which the Hong Kong Listing Rules categorize as a WVR (weighted voting rights) structure. Jack Ma and Joe Tsai are the partnership's continuity partners.

notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (data.js fy 'Mar 2026'). Alibaba reports in renminbi (RMB, ISO code CNY); values are billions of RMB, converted from RMB millions with no FX. Sources are the FY2026 Form 20-F (filed May 20, 2026, accession 0001193125-26-231755); unlike FY2025, it attaches no Hong Kong annual report exhibit. Cash and stock-comp figures match SEC XBRL. LEADER: Jack Ma does not appear in the Item 7.A beneficial ownership table (directors and executive officers, plus anyone known to own 5% or more, as of May 18, 2026, on 18,669,888,147 ordinary shares outstanding). So no current holding is reported, and he is recorded as no-reported-stake. The 20-F's only percentage for him is historical: 'the percentage of our ordinary shares Jack Ma and his affiliates beneficially owned immediately prior to the completion of our initial public offering was 8.8%' (2014), which is not used. It also says that in 2011 he contributed 280,000,000 shares to APN Ltd., a vehicle he set up with Joe Tsai; it does not say what APN holds now. HOLDERS: the table names no 5% holder, so largestHolders is empty; directors and executive officers as a group held 1.9%. STOCK COMP: 14,821 million is the company's 'Total share-based compensation expense', which 'includes both cash and non-cash share-based compensation expenses' (Alibaba Group awards 9,146; subsidiaries' and Ant Group awards 5,675). GEOGRAPHY: null. The 20-F (Note 29 Segment information) states: 'As substantially all of the Company's long-lived assets are located in the PRC and substantially all of the Company's revenue is derived within the PRC, no geographical information is presented.' DIVIDENDS exclude RMB1,317 million paid by non-wholly owned subsidiaries to noncontrolling interests. BUYBACKS fell from RMB86,662 million in fiscal 2025 to RMB7,638 million. PLAN: no broad employee stock purchase plan is described in the sections read.

ecosystem.notes: The FY2026 20-F (year ended March 31, 2026) defines GMV ('the value of paid orders of products and services on our marketplaces, including shipping charges paid by buyers to sellers') and uses it in its take-rate definition, but discloses no GMV total for the group or its marketplaces, so measure is null. The only GMV figure is for Freshippo, a retail business ('Freshippo's overall GMV exceeded RMB 107 billion in fiscal year 2026'), which is not a platform measure. No TPV or other platform volume is reported. Revenue is Alibaba's whole-group revenue (customer management, membership, logistics, cloud, direct sales of goods and more), not only marketplace fees, so it should not be read as a take rate on any merchant volume.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Alibaba revenue is group-wide and no platform volume is disclosed.

taxes.notes: Taxes: us-gaap:IncomeTaxesPaidNet, cash paid for income tax net of refunds received (Chinese mainland 30,729, non-Chinese mainland 3,284, RMB millions). R&D not reported as a separate line. Alibaba reports 'Product development expenses' (RMB66,533 million for FY2026); the 20-F says they consist primarily of staff costs and share-based compensation for research and development personnel and other costs of developing new technologies and products, but it does not say the line is R&D, so it is not recorded under the 'only if the filing says it is R&D' rule.

paidout.notes: Alibaba files its 20-F under US GAAP, so interest and income taxes paid are inside operating cash flow and nothing is added back. Capex is land use rights plus property and equipment (126,063; no companyfacts fact for this combined line) plus intangible assets (874). Income tax paid is now in the income-tax note's composition table (net of refunds, ASU 2023-09). Alibaba is not an admitted marketplace for salesEnabled. The USD column is a convenience translation and is not used. Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026; FX: the calendar-2025 average covers 9 of its 12 months.

marketcap.notes: One class of ordinary shares, listed in Hong Kong (9988, priced in HKD) and traded in New York as ADSs (BABA, one ADS = eight shares); the Hong Kong primary line is used. The count is the HKEX October 2026 monthly return's issued shares excluding treasury shares (the return shows 0 treasury shares, and the September-quarter results announcement of November 19, 2026 says 'As of September 30, 2026, our company did not hold any treasury shares as defined in the Hong Kong Listing Rules'). The FY2026 20-F's count (18,669,888,147 outstanding at May 18, 2026) is stale: in August 2026 Alibaba 'issued 710,000,000 ordinary shares' in a placing (results announcement). Even before the placing, the HKEX count (19,174,988,918 at July 31, 2026) was about 505 million above the 20-F's US GAAP outstanding count; none of the documents read states what the gap is, so the HKEX count is used as stated and may be up to about 2.6% above the US GAAP outstanding basis.

pay.notes: Employees: full-time employees at the March 31, 2026 fiscal year end, from the FY2026 20-F. Payroll is null: the 20-F gives no total of salaries, staff costs or employee benefits (staff costs appear only as components of cost of revenue and operating expense lines; the only aggregate is directors' and executive officers' pay of about RMB250 million), and Alibaba, a foreign private issuer, files no proxy and has no CEO pay ratio. This year's 20-F attaches no Hong Kong annual report exhibit.
